models.title: Inventory turnover
models.summary: Inventory turnover compares cost of goods sold to average inventory.

relationship.original_equation: Inventory turnover = cost of goods sold / average inventory
relationship.translation_notes: Amounts share one currency; the quotient counts turnovers over the declared financial period. Different denominators define different economic measures.

variables.definition: cost of goods sold for the stated period and accounting scope
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

variables.definition: average inventory for the same period and entity
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

variables.definition: Amount of cost of goods sold per unit of average inventory in the stated period
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: The flow and average balance use the same entity, currency, accounting basis and period.
The chosen averaging convention is specified and applied consistently.
limitations: Inventory write-downs and seasonality affect the cost and average-balance measures.
A quarterly turnover is per quarter and must not be compared with an annual turnover without an explicit period adjustment.
